headline: Broad-based sales growth as profit rebounds sharply
summary_short: Baxter's Q2 2026 revenue rose to $2,960M, up 5.3% y/y and 9.6% q/q, while net income rebounded to $126M ($0.24 diluted) from a $15M loss in Q1 2026, even as underlying (ex-special-items) gross margin fell 210bp y/y on higher manufacturing costs and mix.
summary_long: Revenue grew 5.3% y/y and 9.6% q/q to $2,960M, with both segments contributing: Medical Products & Therapies +7% on Advanced Surgery and firmer infusion demand, Healthcare Systems & Technologies +4% on patient-monitoring backlog execution. GAAP gross margin was 34.9%, down from 35.3% y/y; excluding special items it fell 210bp y/y on higher manufacturing/supply costs and mix, partly offset by ~$75M of IEEPA tariff refunds in cost of sales. Net income rebounded to $126M ($0.24 diluted) from a $15M Q1 loss, helped by a smaller special-items drag and a 15% effective tax rate. Cash rose to $2,150M; no shares were repurchased and the dividend held at $0.01/share. No new forward guidance appears in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based: Medical Products & Therapies +7% (Advanced Surgery +12% on hemostats/sealants volume; Infusion Therapies & Platforms +6% on pharmacy-compounding demand and a weak prior-year IV solutions comp), Healthcare Systems & Technologies +4% (Care & Connectivity Solutions +6% on U.S. patient-support-system backlog execution).

Excluding special items, gross margin fell 210bp y/y on higher manufacturing and supply costs (including indirect costs newly capitalized into inventory post-Kidney-Care separation) and unfavorable mix, partly offset by ~$75M of IEEPA tariff refunds booked to cost of sales in Q2.
